entries.title: Bats and how they find their way
entries.answer: Bats are mammals and can fly by flapping their wings. Their wings are made of thin skin stretched over long fingers. Many kinds of bats fly in the dark and use sound to find their way. A bat makes a call and listens for the sound to bounce back. The echo may tell the bat where a moth or a branch is. This is called echolocation. Bats can also see. Many eat insects, but some kinds eat fruit or drink nectar from flowers.
facts: Bats are the only mammals that can fly by flapping their wings.
Some bats can carry pollen between flowers.

entries.title: What makes an ecosystem
entries.answer: An ecosystem includes living things in a place, the parts of the place that are not alive, and the ways they affect one another. Think of a pond. Sunlight reaches plants and algae in the water. Tiny animals feed on algae, and bigger animals may eat those tiny animals. Bacteria and fungi can break down dead material, making some parts of it available for life to use again. The amount of light, warmth, and water can change which living things do well there. A reef, forest, or puddle can each be an ecosystem.
facts: A food web shows more than one path through which living things get food.
Light and water are parts of an ecosystem even though they are not alive.
